content:
A function is continuous at \(x=c\) only if the left-hand limit, right-hand limit, and function value all agree.

Looking at the graph in \([-6,6]\), the only break occurs at \(x=-1\):
- From the left, the graph approaches the open circle at \((-1,3)\), so  
  \[
  \lim_{x\to -1^-}f(x)=3.
  \]
- At \(x=-1\), the filled point is \((-1,-3)\), so  
  \[
  f(-1)=-3.
  \]
- From the right, the curve approaches the same filled point, so  
  \[
  \lim_{x\to -1^+}f(x)=-3.
  \]

Since the left-hand limit is not equal to the right-hand limit, the function is not continuous at \(x=-1\). The red point lies on the continuous curve and does not indicate a break.
